summary_of_task: Test the static personal website pages index.html, blog.html, and resume.html at 1280x720 against the spec: verify navigation reachability, consistent dark styling with readable text and shared nav/footer, landing page content for Avery Hart including robotics/computer vision summary and contact/profile rows, blog page title and realistic previews, resume sections, and check for clipping/overlap. Capture evidence and report issues with severity.
results: I tested the visible GUI behavior of the three pages through the top navigation. The landing page, blog page, and resume page were all reachable via the shared top nav. All pages used a coherent dark charcoal theme with white/light text that was generally readable, and each page included a footer. The landing page showed Avery Hart and a robotics/computer vision-focused summary in the left/profile and main content areas. The blog page had a clear 'Blog Posts' title and multiple realistic post previews. The resume page had clearly labeled Experience, Education, and Projects sections with compact readable entries, plus an additional Interests section. The resume page content fit cleanly within the 1280x720 viewport without overlap.
important_findings:
1. Medium severity: On the landing page at 1280x720, important content is clipped/truncated rather than fully visible. The lower portion of the main text/link block is cut off above the footer, and the expected contact/profile list is incomplete in the visible layout: Email, ORCID, and GitHub are visible, but LinkedIn is not visible in the viewport. Attempting to scroll did not reveal additional page content, suggesting a layout-height/clipping issue rather than normal page overflow. Evidence captured in screenshots 001 and 002.
2. Low severity: On blog.html, the post preview list is displayed inside a fixed-height inner scroll region with its own scrollbar. This does allow more content, but the lowest visible post title in the initial view is partially clipped, so not all preview content is immediately readable without scrolling inside the panel. Evidence captured in screenshot 003.
3. Pass: resume.html matched the required content well for the tested items. Experience, Education, and Projects were visible, readable, and not clipped or overlapping at 1280x720. Evidence captured in screenshot 004.
suggestions: Adjust the landing page layout height/spacing so the full main text and all required contact/profile rows, including LinkedIn, are visible at 1280x720 without truncation. On the blog page, consider increasing the visible height of the preview list or avoiding the nested scroll container so more previews are readable in the initial viewport.
other_notes: Navigation clicks caused page transitions successfully despite transient tool messages indicating navigation context changes. No file modifications were made. Findings are based only on observed visible behavior.
